text: Add a low-rank user-item interaction term to the existing additive logits: represent each known user and video with 16-dimensional embeddings and score each impression as bias plus additive user/item weights plus their embedding dot product, while retaining pointwise binary cross-entropy training and the current data split. This tests whether personalized user-video affinity improves within-user ordering over the additive-only model without changing labels or evaluation.
rationale: The interaction term can distinguish videos for a user even when additive user and item effects cannot, directly targeting the official primary mean of GAUC and nDCG@5. Compare primary first, then inspect GAUC, nDCG@5, and ranking diagnostics such as Precision@5, MAP@5, MRR@5, Recall@5, and HitRate@5 to determine whether gains are concentrated at the top of the list. Classification metrics and threshold behavior diagnose whether any ranking change reflects improved class separation, while positive_rate and score spread detect collapse or instability.
